info.bio:
NoMeansNo es una respetada e influyente banda de punk canadiense, originaria de Victoria, British Columbia. La banda se forma en 1979 por los hermanos John y Rob Wright quienes practicaban en el sótano de la casa de sus padres.

scenes.name: Hardcore
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El punk como «violento, rápido y ruidoso» tarda en conquistar EE UU, pero cuando lo hace el hardcore se convierte durante dos décadas en el idioma nacional de millones de chavales. Misfits y el «scum-rock»; el crossover punk-metal (Suicidal Tendencies, Corrosion Of Conformity, Agnostic Front); Mission Of Burma en Boston. Washington: Bad Brains (reggae, funk y metal diez años por delante), Minor Threat (el «straight-edge») y Rites Of Spring, inventores del emo-core. San Francisco: Dead Kennedys de Jello Biafra, D.R.I. (thrash antes que Metallica), Flipper. Los «beach punks» de Los Ángeles: Germs, X, Black Flag (Damaged), Descendents, Gun Club (Fire Of Love), Bad Religion. El jazz-core de Minutemen y Saccharine Trust; en el Medio Oeste, Husker Du y Replacements cambian el hardcore para siempre; en Chicago, Naked Raygun y Big Black de Steve Albini; en Europa, The Ex y los italianos CCCP.

podcast.title: Artwork Designer
podcast.body: Peter Saville, chief art design guy at Factory Records, did design work for No Means No (referred to as "Noam D" in the transcript). "He did everything from gig posters to album design for Joy Division New Order, Roxas music, Swade, pulp, Martha Nemuffins, and Noam D."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Genre Blending and Influence
podcast.body: NoMeansNo occupied a unique space by blending elements of hardcore and metal. Their sound contained elements that would later define post-hardcore, influencing bands like At the Drive-In, Rollins Band, Alexisonfire, Billy Talent, Deftones, and Silverstein. "They ended up occupying a space somewhere between hardcore and metal. If you listen carefully to what they did, you can hear elements of what would become known as post-hardcore, a sound that would later birth groups like at the drive-in, Rollins Band, Alexis on Fire, Billy Talent, The Death Tones and Silverstein."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Geographical Origins and Evolution
podcast.body: No Means No originated in Victoria, Canada, and later relocated to Vancouver. Their sound occupied a unique space blending hardcore and metal, and they are recognized for containing elements that would later define post-hardcore. "And then there was no means no, who started in Victoria and later moved to Vancouver. They ended up occupying a space somewhere between hardcore and metal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Iconic Vancouver Hardcore Band
podcast.body: No Means No is recognized as a prominent band from Vancouver's 70s and 80s hardcore scene, which was a defining musical characteristic of the city during that era. Matthew Good referenced them while discussing the loss of Vancouver's influential musical "edge." "I can't see no means no or DOA or adversity or anyone doing that."

podcast.title: Van Theft & Polish Mafia (Poland)
podcast.body: While on tour in Poland one Christmas, NoMeansNo had their rented van stolen after a show in Warsaw, containing about $10,000 worth of merchandise. With local police being unhelpful and the Dutch rental company concerned about insurance coverage outside Holland, a fan connected them with the Polish Mafia. Band member Rob Wright met two heavily armed men in a church basement and negotiated the van's return for 2000 German marks. The next day, the van and all its contents were recovered from a barn outside Warsaw. However, the Warsaw police later demanded another 2000 German marks for operating outside legal channels. "The next day the van was given the name of a village about 100 kilometers outside of Warsaw and told to wait in the town square."

podcast.title: Victoria Band History
podcast.body: NoMeansNo is identified as a "fine Canadian punk band" from Victoria, British Columbia, who have been active since the late 1970s. The band is known for insisting on doing things their own way, which sometimes leads them into trouble. "no means no, a fine Canadian punk band from Victoria who have been around since the late 1970s."
